series: SAE Exercises and Games of Judgment / 判断力练习与游戏
scope: Four complete public-facing essays in English and both Chinese scripts, not full translations of the four technical papers.
method: All four source papers read in full; published HTTPS bytes verified identical to the author's source checkout. The JSON manuscripts are the independent publication text. No external translation service.
editorial_boundaries: A judgment is a discovery of a possibility not exhausted by the current rules or framing. Prediction supplies material; action is distinct. Changed action or outcome does not prove practice or improvement.
Play is one route for the exercise of judgment, not the only route or a duty. No claim that repeated play makes people better, produces lasting improvement, or transfers outside the game.

The arrangement of play and the participant's stance are separate. Solo, competitive and cooperative play are not moral ranks. Coordination, applause, handshakes, or successful cooperation cannot by themselves establish recognition.

A person's reason for seeking practice does not remove play. Work and play can coexist in one event. Gambling is excluded by this inquiry's scope convention; pure chance and pooled entry fees remain unresolved boundary cases.

Voluntary entry and a usable exit matter. Manipulating exit can remain objectionable while the participant is still playing; neither an exit button nor long play alone settles whether exit is genuinely available.

Cooperation invites recognition without guaranteeing it. A partner cannot be reduced to material for one's moral improvement; recognition cannot be produced by coercing oneself. Having one's own goals is not incompatible with regard for another person.

Writing anticipates a reader without making the imagined reader an actual second subject. The eventual reader's judgment remains their own. Diaries and when writing constitutes a completed cooperative game are not treated as settled.
Closing invitations are optional, unscored observations, not psychological tests or behavioral prescriptions. No developmental age, clinical benefit, or empirical training result is asserted.
